Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Pulla Karthik
 Writ Petition No.2388 Of 2023
Order:

(per AKS,J) Smt. Yellamma, the petitioner, has filed this Habeas Corpus petition on behalf of her husband, Dakoori Biksham, S/o. Lachaiah, the detenu, challenging the detention order vide C.No.60/WRC/CSB-XI/2023, dated 21.01.2023, passed by the respondent No.2-Commissioner of Police, Warangal, whereby, the detenu was detained under Section 3(2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug- Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders,
Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders,
Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (for short, 'Act 1 of 1986'),
and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.363, General Administration (Spl. (Law &
Order)) Department, dated 08.03.2023, passed by the Secretary to Government, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order)) Department, Government of Telangana.
2

sentences.text: AKS,J & PK,J 2.

Heard Ms. R. Sowmya Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri S. Mujib Kumar, learned Special Government Pleader, representing the learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondents.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner had contended that the detenu was detained by the respondents vide impugned detention order, dated 21.01.2023, by invoking the provisions under the Act 1 of 1986 on the alleged ground that he was involved in six crimes i.e. Crime Nos.221 of 2022 and 222 of 2022 of Rayaparthy Police Station, registered for the offences under Sections 420, 468 and 471 I.P.C; Crime No.629 of 2022 of A.J. Mills Colony Police Station, registered for the offences under Sections 420 and 468 I.P.C.; Crime No.630 of 2022 of A.J. Mills Colony Police Station,
Warangal Commissionerate, registered for the offence under Section 420 I.P.C.; Crime No.294 of 2022 of Dornakal Police Station, Mahabubabad District, registered for the offences under Sections 406, 468 and 471 read with 34 I.P.C.; and Crime No.357 of 2022 of Khammam I Town Police Station, Khammam District, registered for the offence under Section 420 I.P.C.

sentences.text: The detenu was granted bail in Crime Nos.221 of 2022, 222 of 2022, 629 of 2022 and 630 of 2022 and
in the remaining two crimes i.e. Crime Nos.294 of 2022 and 357 of 2022, the bail applications moved by the detenu are still pending.
Thus, the detenu continues to be in judicial custody as on the date of passing of the impugned detention order.
The detaining authority, without application of mind, has passed the impugned detention order on the ground that the detenu is causing inconvenience and disturbance to the general public.
Learned counsel further contended that when the detenu is in jail on judicial remand, the question of the detenu disturbing the peace and tranquility in the society would not arise.
The impugned orders are passed without application of mind.

Therefore, appropriate orders be passed in the Writ Petition by setting aside the impugned orders, as admittedly, as on the date of passing of the impugned detention order, the detenu is in judicial remand.

5. On the other hand, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents had contended that the detenu was involved in six crimes of serious nature and there is every possibility of the detenu being enlarged on bail.
Therefore, the respondents 4 AKS,J & PK,J were justified in passing the impugned orders to ensure that the public at large are not disturbed with the activities of the detenu.
There are no merits in the Writ Petition and the same is liable to be dismissed.

6. This Court, having considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties,
is of the view that since the detenu is in judicial remand as on the date of passing of the impugned detention order, the question of detenu disturbing the public would not arise.

Therefore, the impugned detention order, dated 21.01.2023, and the consequential confirmation order, dated 08.03.2023, are liable to be set aside, as admittedly, as on the date of passing of the impugned detention order, the detenu was in judicial remand.
8. In the result, the Writ Petition is allowed.

The impugned detention order vide C.No.60/WRC/CSB-XI/2023, dated 21.01.2023, passed by the respondent No.2, and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.363, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order))
Department, dated 08.03.2023, passed by the Secretary to Government, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order)) Department, Government of Telangana, are hereby set aside.
However, it is made clear that since the detenu is in judicial remand, 5 AKS,J & PK,J the question of setting free the detenu would not arise.
However, the detenu would be entitled to get released, if the competent criminal Courts grant bail to him in the crimes registered against him.
There shall be no order as to costs.

Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.
___________________________ ABHINAND KUMAR SHAVILI, J _________________ PULLA KARTHIK, J Date: 27-03-2023.
